body: Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 head 0d218990 (six commits on main b9209774; 30 files, +415/-1731). Re-derived from the diff: home/dot_mise/config.toml requests latest for every tool except fd, npm:pnpm, http:bats and http:gcloud, each with a reason comment; [settings] drops lockfile, locked and lockfile_platforms and sets minimum_release_age = 7d plus self_update.minimum_release_age = 7d; mise.lock and the mise.lock.tmpl are deleted and .chezmoiremove lists .config/mise/mise.lock so hosts drop the stale copy; the manifest's mise-tools asset entry is gone with the validator line that required it; Makefile update runs scripts/upgrade-tools.sh (SYSTEM=1 adds apt) in place of the two locked installs and the upgrade target is deleted; install/common/mise.sh, scripts/update-agent-assets.sh and install/common/sheldon.sh lose --locked and the per-command --before flags (the npm min_release_age bypass for the agent CLIs stays, --force stays only in the broken-CLI repair path, which returns early when the CLI runs); scripts/upgrade-tools.sh points MISE_CONFIG_DIR at the applied host config, keeps MISE_CEILING_PATHS at the checkout root (Bot 4229677547, proved with mise config ls: without the ceiling a parent mise.toml joins the inventory), deletes the T117 guard, apply_upgraded_mise_config, bump_terminal_tool_pins, upgrade_agent_assets and upgrade_agent_cli_tools (which bypassed the cooldown and wrote an exact pin into the applied config), runs mise self-update and mise upgrade without --bump, sets HOMEBREW_NO_ASK=1 (Bot 4229994970), exits 0 under CI=true, and keeps the release-asset pin helpers unwired for T119 (ponytail comment); the statusline CI job installs from the copied config and compares physical paths and mise current versions (check-statusline-tools.py takes the versions as arguments); renovate.json drops the lock-fidelity rule and holds npm:pnpm beside fd (Bot 4229994961); default.rules drops make upgrade; the launcher directive drops the pin-diff words; README states the policy with the four citations, the backend coverage of the cooldown, the live node probe, the trade-offs (machines may differ, CI tests the latest safe set, global lockfile mode no longer set for other projects, node major bumps and npm tools), the holding-back mechanisms and the make update failure behaviour; the SKILL pins clause and the boundary-check pins wording are gone; tests rewritten to the new policy (supply-chain, statusline, runtime-health host-config and CI-skip cases, herdr-agents Makefile and directive strings, lifecycle.bats greps, mise.bats, sheldon.bats, ua-core pnpm assertion). CI 16 of 16 on 0d218990; Codex Bot reviewed earlier heads (three P2 threads, all fixed at root cause per the operator's standing instruction) and completed with no findings on 0d218990; all three threads replied to and resolved by the orchestrator; sweep at 0d218990: 18 items, every one dispositioned. Known leftovers named in the report: the Claude hook pair (routed to a Codex seat), T119's files, and the zshrc claude-update helper now bounded by the cooldown. Orchestrator-run network probes (Amendment 2) are pasted in the validation file with attribution.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-1 head 9a7a6ca0 (three commits on 0d218990; 7 files, +117/-72). Re-derived from the diff: the network-only phases (Homebrew, mise self-update, uv tools, gh extensions) run as run_optional_phase so an offline host still converges, while installing the declared mise tools stays required; the install step is one bare mise install --yes (a per-tool install re-resolves latest over the network and fails offline, shown by the worker's offline probe in validation section 12) and upgrades stay per tool with the http: and fd skips; minimum_release_age and self_update.minimum_release_age are 72h (operator decision on the orchestrator's research: pnpm 'within an hour', the 24-hour defaults of mise and pnpm 11, the multi-day Shai-Hulud waves, and the cost of delaying security fixes); HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1 is exported for the brew phase when gh is on PATH, with one skip line otherwise; README carries the three anchors, the Homebrew attestation sentence, the offline-convergence behaviour and 72 hours everywhere; tests: the no-gh case hides the runner's own gh, a failing fake brew leaves exit 0 and the mise phase runs, the attestation env is asserted, lifecycle.bats greps the literal update lines, supply-chain and statusline tests follow 72h. CI 16 of 16 on 9a7a6ca0; Bot completed with no findings on 9a7a6ca0; the three earlier threads stay fixed and resolved; sweep at 9a7a6ca0: 18 items, every one dispositioned. The agent-CLI exclusion, the npm provenance check and the Claude Code channel move are T120 by the operator's decision.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-2 head b6e27bd7 (two commits on 9a7a6ca0; 6 files, +53/-10). Re-derived from the diff: the update target now ends its pull step with @$(MAKE) --no-print-directory update-tree, and update-tree (chezmoi applies, upgrade-tools.sh, update-agent-assets.sh, the Herdr reload, agmsg-bootstrap) is read from the Makefile the pull just fetched, so a recipe change lands in the same run; SYSTEM reaches it through MAKEFLAGS; make apply is unchanged; the worker's scratch proof (validation 14) shows the base recipe, the new recipe, and a pull that brings a recipe change in commit C executing C's update-tree in the same run; README states the split and the one-time git pull && make update note for hosts still on the old Makefile. In upgrade-tools.sh the per-tool mise upgrade loop returns 2 on a tool failure and the phase counts it as an optional warning while the bare mise install --yes and the tool listing stay required; a new test (install ok, upgrade fails) asserts exit 0 with the warning. The report's review-record count now matches the artifact (24, read by jq). CI on 9514a3cd failed one Makefile test outside the round's list (test_codex_config_merge), fixed in b6e27bd7 after the full local suite showed no branch-only failure. CI 16 of 16 on b6e27bd7; Bot completed with no findings on 9514a3cd and none on the test-only head b6e27bd7; the three earlier threads stay fixed and resolved; sweep at b6e27bd7: 18 items, every one dispositioned. The three audit findings of 9a7a6ca0 are fixed at root cause in 9514a3cd (the two P2) and the report (the P3).

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 rounds 3 and 4: heads 94f4af69 (audit findings of b6e27bd7: make update-tree added to the Codex execpolicy forbidden list with its test; the README node-major sentence; the report), b621af77 (Bot P2s on 94f4af69: npm: tools reinstalled with mise install --force when node moved, mise self-update --no-plugins), f25e9eaf (Codex seat T121: the Claude hook recovery hint and its test, because a Claude seat does not edit its own boundary), 64c6d8a6 (Bot P2s on f25e9eaf: README three entry points, fd hold by matchDepNames, npm_config_min_release_age=3 aligned with the 72-hour cooldown for every npm: tool rather than an agent-only zero, keeping a 3-day gate on transitive dependencies) and the round-4 head 88e369d9 (the two Bot P2s on b621af77 the round-3 RESULT had left unnamed: the node snapshot moved before the bare install, with a test where the install itself moves node; MISE_CONFIG_DIR fixed to $HOME/.config/mise, the chezmoi target, never inherited and independent of XDG_CONFIG_HOME, with the host-config test covering both). Re-derived from the diffs; both round-4 tests fail against the 64c6d8a6 script (validation 19). Scope deviation recorded: tests/unit/test_codex_config_merge.py was changed in b6e27bd7 before its amendment (the orchestrator's miss; amended in round 3). CI 16 of 16 on 88e369d9 (one ubuntu-26.04 attempt stalled in bats and was rerun); Bot completed with no findings on 88e369d9; all eleven threads named one to one against the PR listing (validation 10), replied to and resolved by the orchestrator; sweep at 88e369d9: every item dispositioned.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-5 head 5d991b47 (one commit on 88e369d9). Re-derived from the diff: after the forced reinstall of npm: tools that follows a node move, the mise phase runs the bare mise install --yes once more as the required step, so a tool that a failed --force removed is reinstalled or the phase fails; the reinstall loop's own failure stays a warning because that final install decides. Two new tests model the install marker with a fake mise (a --force that deletes the install and exits 1 followed by a successful bare install → exit 0 and the tool present; the final install failing → exit 1), and both fail against the 88e369d9 script (validation 20). README's reinstall sentence and the report's claim about an unavailable declared tool are aligned. CI 16 of 16 on 5d991b47; Bot completed with no findings on 5d991b47; all eleven threads stay resolved; sweep at 5d991b47: every item dispositioned.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-6 head eee788f0 (two commits on 5d991b47; 6 files, +149/-63). Re-derived from the diff: home/dot_npmrc min-release-age=3 is the single npm age policy, equal to mise's 72 hours, the per-script export is gone and the installer's npm lines follow, with a test tying the npmrc days to the mise setting; the in-process node snapshot is replaced by a persistent marker (${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/dotfiles/npm-tools-node) compared with mise current node after the install and upgrade steps, so a node moved by the installer or an earlier run is seen; the rebuild of each npm: tool is non-destructive (moved aside, installed at its exact version, restored on failure, no --force), the final bare mise install --yes decides convergence, the marker is written only after a complete rebuild and that install, and an unwritable marker fails the phase (the two Bot P2s on d0dd981d, fixed in eee788f0); tests cover marker differs, final install fails after a rebuild, and marker unwritable, and they fail against the previous scripts (validation 21, 22); README's reinstall paragraph names the marker and the non-destructive rebuild. CI 16 of 16 on eee788f0; Bot completed with no findings on eee788f0; all thirteen threads named one to one (validation 10), replied to and resolved by the orchestrator; sweep at eee788f0: 52 items, every one dispositioned.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-7 head 408727c9 (on eee788f0). Re-derived from the diff: the non-destructive rebuild sets INT/TERM/EXIT traps right after the move-aside that restore the previous install (exit 130/143) and clears them once the exact install returns; a backup left by a killed run is restored rather than deleted; the test has the fake mise signal the script and fails against eee788f0 (143 vs -15). install/common/mise.sh is mise trust followed by one bare mise install: the per-tool lines and the agent-CLI npm min-release-age bypass are gone (their per-group cooldowns no longer exist, ~/.npmrc carries the one policy), mise.bats follows, and the supply-chain test asserts no bypass in the installer. The validation greps of sections 21 and 22 are replaced by grep -F with complete output and the abbreviated commands of sections 19 to 22 rerun in full (23.4); the earlier omission came from a shell grep alias reading ${ as an anchor. Remaining npm_config_min_release_age=0 uses: the .zshrc claude-update helper (T120 retires it) and the update-agent-assets.sh broken-CLI repair path (immediate repair of a missing CLI, kept). CI 16 of 16 on 408727c9 (one ubuntu-24.04 bats stall cancelled and rerun); Bot completed with no findings on 408727c9; all thirteen threads stay resolved; sweep at 408727c9: every item dispositioned.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-8 head 61c38cd6 (f79d7b4e, 61c38cd6 on 408727c9). Re-derived from the diff: restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds runs first in the mise phase, before mise trust and the bare install, scanning <installs>/*/*.before-node-rebuild with the installs directory resolved as MISE_INSTALLS_DIR, then MISE_DATA_DIR, then XDG_DATA_HOME/mise (mise's own order), so a backup left by a SIGKILLed run is back before mise is asked to name the tool; rebuild_mise_npm_tool no longer restores itself and refuses to move an install aside while a backup exists; after a successful exact install the backup is renamed to a dot-named discard directory before deletion, so an undeletable backup can never be mistaken for an interrupted rebuild on the next run and mise ls does not list it (worker probe 25.3 shows a non-dot leftover listed as a version, the dot-named one not). Tests: three subtests (install dir absent, partial, custom MISE_INSTALLS_DIR) with an offline fake mise whose bare install fails unless the backup is restored first, and an undeletable-backup test running the script twice; both fail against f79d7b4e per validation 25.4. Bot threads on f79d7b4e: 4234006744 and 4234006752 fixed in 61c38cd6 (verified in the diff); 4234006735 (offline bare install under minimum_release_age) refuted: the orchestrator reproduced the worker's probe independently in the network-less sandbox with mise 2026.9.17, minimum_release_age 72h and 720h, an empty MISE_CACHE_DIR and an installed jq@latest: 'already installed', rc=0, no metadata fetched; a tool that is not installed fails offline as documented. Residual exposure: the behaviour is that of the installed mise, which self-updates; a later mise that fetches metadata for installed fuzzy requests would surface as a required failure offline, not as data loss. Codex Bot on 61c38cd6 completed with no findings; CI 16 of 16; every thread replied to and resolved by the orchestrator. Verdict: send to the task-level audit.

Orchestrator adversarial review of PR #310 round-9 head a9eb7f02 (one commit on 61c38cd6). Re-derived from the diff: restore_npm_install moves the backup only when rm -rf succeeded and the old path is gone, otherwise prints 'required failure: could not restore <install> from <backup>', increments required_failures and returns 1; restore_interrupted_npm_rebuilds continues past a failed restore and returns 1 if any failed, so the phase fails and the operator sees every path to repair; the trap and the rebuild-failure path share the same helper, so an interrupted rebuild whose partial install cannot be deleted also fails loudly instead of burying the backup. Test models the killed-rebuild state with a read-only directory inside the partial install (skipped as root, mode restored in finally), asserts the backup still holds 'original', nothing moved into the partial directory, exit 1 and the message naming both paths; it fails against 61c38cd6 (validation 26.1). Evidence: section 26.2 reruns the section-17 grep exactly as printed at 64c6d8a6 and shows the separate npmrc grep that produced min-release-age=7; 26.3 reruns the section-14 scratch proof with the unprinted grep -E filter removed and complete make -n transcripts; the header names a9eb7f02. CI 16 of 16; Codex Bot completed on a9eb7f02 with no new threads; 0 unresolved threads; sweep 64 items all dispositioned at a9eb7f02. Verdict: send to the task-level audit.
